newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Gulf official sees no threats from Iran.
newsitem.headline: Gulf official sees no threats from Iran.

text.p: Iran did not pose a threat to its Gulf Arab neighbours, a senior Gulf official was on Tuesday quoted as saying.

"I can't say there is a danger coming out of Iran. I don't believe in this (danger)," Jameel al-Hujailan, Secretary-General of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), told the London-based Ashraq al-Awsat newspaper.

Relations between the GCC states -- Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates -- are often tense. The six states had voiced concern over Iran's armament programme and accused it of interfering in their internal affairs.

But Iran has recently taken moves towards improving its ties with its neighbours. Hopes for better relations between non-Arab Iran and the GCC have risen after the election of President Mohammad Khatami, seen as a moderate.

"Iran knows well its interests in the region. It is a big neighbouring country and we are fully anxious in maintaining good relations based on good intentions," Hujailan said. "It's impossible for me to say that Iran forms a danger for the GCC."
Hujailan said the GCC states did not want relations between Iran and the United States to remain strained because that had negative impacts on the stability of the Gulf region.
"We want our region to be safe, far from international struggles," he said.

"Iran is a big and strong neighbour. Iran represents a major factor behind stability in the region. Agreeing with Iran and deepening its conviction on the need to cooperation with the GCC is important to stability in the region," he added.
